newsitem.title: FRANCE: Cr Lyonnais shares jump on profit hopes.
newsitem.headline: Cr Lyonnais shares jump on profit hopes.

text.p: Investors piled into non-voting shares of state-controlled Credit Lyonnais on Thursday after a newspaper report that the long ailing bank expected to produce a sharp recovery in profits in 1997.
At 1259 GMT, the shares were up 6.65 percent at 199.0 francs after hitting a high of 205.1 francs earlier in the day.

Some analysts said they believed the shares could go much higher but cautioned a lot would depend on the government's restructuring plan to ready the bank for privatisation and said they were still a speculative play.

The plan is expected to involve a recapitalisation estimated at between 10 and 15 billion francs to boost the bank's solvency ratios. Analysts believe the new capital is most likely to involve a shares-for-cash exchange.

One brokerage had a worst-case scenario involving asset writedowns plus maximum new share issuance that valued the share at 134 francs. Its best case, involving no writedowns and minimum share issuance, put the stock value at 409 francs.
The shares have been rising steadily over past couple of months amid increasing optimism about the bank's outlook but the latest gains were triggered by the article in Les Echos.
It said the bank expects to report a net attributable profit of 3.4 to 3.7 billion francs in 1997 after a profit of close to 300 million francs for 1996.

The bank, which lost 21 billion francs between 1992 and 1994 as a result of reckless lending spree, declined comment on the figures which the newspaper said had been presented at a December board meeting.

The bright prospects were due to a strong contribution from market activities, good results at the U.S. and Asian businesses, and a rebound in the retail banking network in France, the newspaper said.
